definitions.explanation: A person sent to deliver a message, carry out a mission, or represent someone. Used in historical, literary, and formal modern contexts.

examples.japanese: {使者|ししゃ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{和平|わへい}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{条件|じょうけん}→条件：03285_jouken⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{伝|つた}えた→伝える：01220_tsutaeru⟧。
examples.english: The envoy conveyed the conditions for peace.

examples.japanese: ⟦{春|はる}→春：00627_haru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{訪|おとず}れ→訪れ：14267_otozure⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{告|つ}げる→告げる：11808_tsugeru⟧{使者|ししゃ}⟦のように→のように：30291_noyouni⟧、⟦{梅|うめ}→梅：01869_ume⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{花|はな}→花：00523_hana⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{咲|さ}いた→咲く：08150_saku⟧。
examples.english: The plum blossoms bloomed, like messengers heralding the arrival of spring.

notes:
Compound of {使|し} (to send on a mission) + ⟦{者|しゃ}→〜者：04662_sha⟧ (person). Commonly appears in historical narratives, fantasy, and literary writing. Also used figuratively for things that herald or signal something.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {使者|ししゃ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{送|おく}る→送る：00742_okuru⟧: to send a messenger
- {使者|ししゃ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{遣|つか}わす: to dispatch an envoy (literary)
- {使者|ししゃ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{来|く}る→来る：00254_kuru⟧: a messenger comes
- ⟦{春|はる}→春：00627_haru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{使者|ししゃ}: herald of spring
- ⟦{死|し}→死：13248_shi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{使者|ししゃ}: messenger of death

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{特使|とくし}→特使：23491_tokushi⟧: special envoy — specifically appointed for a particular mission
- ⟦{大使|たいし}→大使：03391_taishi⟧: ambassador — a permanent diplomatic representative
- メッセンジャー: messenger — the loanword, used in modern/casual contexts

NOTE ON HOMOPHONES:
{使者|ししゃ} (messenger) is distinct from ⟦{死者|ししゃ}→死者：13225_shisha⟧ (deceased person). The kanji make the difference clear in writing.
